Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Steve Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, VP of Exploration; and Tom Reilly, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved notable progress in our exploration and drilling activities, with key well results exceeding expectations and clear plans for future growth. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on capital expenditure management, where we came in under budget across key categories while maintaining high efficiency. We are focused on adding proved reserves organically, achieving a robust replacement ratio that underscores our long-term sustainability. Further, we are working on optimizing our refining segment, with record throughput and strong margins. We continue to adjust to advancing our ESG initiatives, making significant strides in emissions reductions. Finally, we are taking steps to unlock future development plans and resource potential across our premier assets.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Steve Harlan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.5 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Operating income was $650 million, and net income was $450 million. We generated $800 million in free cash flow and returned $300 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in debt and $1.5 billion in cash.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. Today I'll dive into our capital expenditure performance, focusing on the drilling, completion, and facilities breakdown—budget versus actual. As you know, our 2023 full-year capex guidance remains at $2.4 billion, weighted 85% towards high-return drilling and completion activities, with the balance on facilities and other infrastructure. This quarter, we spent $620 million on capex, tracking 5% under our quarterly budget of $650 million, driven by operational efficiencies and supply chain optimizations amid softer service costs. Year-to-date, we're at $1.75 billion versus a $1.85 billion budget—about 5.4% under—positioning us well to return meaningful free cash flow at current WTI prices around $82 per barrel.

Let me break this down category by category, with regional insights and the key drivers behind variances. All figures are in millions unless noted otherwise.

Drilling came in at $355 million actual versus $380 million budgeted for Q3, a 6.6% underspend. Year-to-date drilling spend is $1.05 billion versus $1.12 billion planned—a solid 6.3% underspend. This category represents 57% of our total capex pie, concentrated in the Permian Delaware Basin at 70% of activity and Eagle Ford at 25%, with emerging pads in the Bakken. In the Permian Delaware, we averaged 1.85 days per 1,000-foot interval across our 12 active rigs, beating our budget by 12% thanks to optimized bottom-hole assemblies with Schlumberger's GeoSphere directional drilling tech and Weatherford's Hammerdrill percussive tools. This shaved $15 million off costs on 45 drilled wells. Lateral lengths averaged 11,500 feet, up 8% year-over-year, allowing us to capture more Tier 1 inventory per pad—our Midland-to-Delaware breakevens remain sub-$45 per barrel. In Eagle Ford, rig count held steady at 3 rigs, but we deferred two non-core vertical wells amid high gas prices, saving $8 million. Actual AFE costs came in at $7.2 million per horizontal well versus $7.8 million budgeted. Minor delays from Halliburton's Q2 supply chain hiccups on PDC bits pushed $2 million into Q4, but overall, drilling intensity is up 15% year-over-year with no safety incidents. Strategically, we're prioritizing multi-well pad drilling to minimize surface footprint—our five-well pads in the Delaware are yielding 20% better EURs per foot drilled, aligning with our inventory life of 10+ years at sub-$50 breakevens.

Completion spend hit $185 million against $200 million planned for Q3, a 7.5% underspend, with year-to-date at $530 million versus $570 million budgeted—7% under. This is 29% of total capex, heavily skewed to slickwater fracs in the Permian at 75% and hybrid fracs in Eagle Ford. We pumped 2,200 lbs per foot proppant intensity on average, flat to budget, but secured bulk pricing from Hi-Crush at $55 per ton—10% below guidance—saving $12 million. Fluid systems shifted to SLB's SpectraStim viscoelastic diverter, reducing stage counts by 5% on 30 wells without EUR degradation. In the Permian, our Wylie pad—8 wells—came in at $6.5 million per well completed, 9% under budget, thanks to electric frack fleets from Patterson-UTI—cutting 25% of emissions and diesel costs. Eagle Ford saw a 4-well completion deferred to Q4 for better pricing, trimming $5 million. Bakken pilots with Chevron's nano-proppant tech tested successfully, but scaled minimally this quarter. Cycle times down to 7.2 days per well from 8.0 budgeted, driven by zipper fracs across 3 pads. Despite OT inflation stabilizing at 2.5% quarter-over-quarter, we're 15% more efficient than peers like Pioneer per McKinsey benchmarks. These savings fund our digital twin initiatives with Baker Hughes JewelSuite, modeling frac hits to boost parent-child well performance—critical as we stack 40+ wells per section in core acreage.

Facilities were the lone overage this quarter: $80 million spent versus $70 million budgeted, a 14.3% overrun, with year-to-date $170 million versus $160 million—a 6.3% overrun but only 10% of total capex. Primarily tied to Permian midstream tie-ins at 60% and Eagle Ford water infrastructure at 30%. In Permian, we accelerated $6 million on our Delaware Central Gathering system expansion—adding 50 MMcf per day capacity with Enterprise Partners JV—to handle IP rates from new pads averaging 1,800 boe per day. Also, $4 million overrun on SWD wells due to EPA-mandated liners amid produced water volumes up 20% year-over-year. Eagle Ford and ESG push added $3 million extra for recycled water facilities using XRI's Blue Water tech, supporting 85% reuse rates and our net-zero Scope 1 goals by 2030. Bakken electrification pilots added $2 million. Offsets included deferring $2 million in non-essential leases. Forward-looking, facilities capex accelerates in Q4 to $90 million for CCUS injection hubs, partnering with Occidental's STRATOS project—tax credits under 45Q will offset 30% of costs.

Total D&C underspend of $112 million year-to-date gives us dry powder for bolt-on M&A, like our recent $150 million DJ Basin tuck-in mirroring Continental Resources' playbook. Service cost deflation persists—drilling down 8%, completions 6%—but we're hedging 60% of 2024 activity at $75 per barrel equivalent. Q4 capex guidance: $580-620 million, full-year reaffirmation at $2.4 billion, generating $450-550 million FCF at strip prices. This discipline sustains our 12% yield and $1.2 billion buyback authorization.

Before moving on, a quick note on proved reserves additions, a core value driver for sustaining multi-decade production profiles. For full-year 2023 so far, we're on track to add over 1.2 billion barrels of oil equivalent in proved reserves, up 18% from 2022 levels, bringing year-end to around 8.7 billion boe and providing a 17-year reserve life at our 500 million boe annual production rate. Our total reserve replacement ratio is targeting 240%, with organic RRR at 185%—organic additions of 925 million boe against production. Extensions and discoveries drove 65% of additions at 780 million boe, positive revisions another 250 million boe from strong well performance in shale assets, improved recovery 120 million boe from EOR pilots, and purchases 50 million boe. In Permian—45% of reserves—we're replacing 110% organically with 350 million boe added via infill on 450,000 net acres. Horizontal laterals at 12,000 feet and super-spec fracs unlocked 25% EUR uplift in Wolfcamp A and Second Bone Springs. Eagle Ford hit 220% organic RRR, adding 200 million boe through black oil extensions. Internationally, offshore Namibia added 150 million boe, de-risking 2 billion boe gross mean, and North Sea 100 million boe via polymer flood EOR. Our three-year organic RRR averages 175%, with finding costs at $8.50 per boe, 20% below peers. This positions us for 5-7% annual organic growth through the decade.

On refining, our downstream delivered robust performance amid WTI at $82 and Brent at $85 from OPEC+ cuts and demand recovery. We processed a record 1.28 million barrels per day, up 8% year-over-year, at 96% utilization above our 92% target. Gulf Coast Port Arthur at 98% utilization hit 850,000 bpd on sour crudes; Midwest Whiting 92% at 380,000 bpd; West Coast Martinez 85% at 50,000 bpd. Exports surged 15% to 250,000 bpd of ULSD and jet. Realized net crack spread averaged $28.50 per barrel, up 22% year-over-year, outpacing NYMEX 3-2-1 at $24.80. Gasoline at $22, diesel $35, jet $42; yields 108% of input, distillates 52%. Generated $45 million in RINs from renewable diesel co-processing. Cash op costs $5.80 per barrel, down 6%, via AI-driven APC and post-turnaround gains. Advancing $1.2 billion Port Arthur expansion for 50,000 bpd renewable diesel by 2025.

I will now turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Steve. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Lightning Bolt 12H-15H online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Thank you, Steve, and good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our exploration and drilling activity updates, where we continue to execute with discipline and deliver strong results across our high-return assets. Our strategy remains laser-focused on capital efficiency, maximizing returns on Tier 1 inventory, and extending the inventory life of our key basins to well over a decade. In Q3, we spudded 28 wells and brought online 32 wells, with our drilling and completion capex coming in at $450 million, right in line with our full-year guidance of $1.8 to $2.0 billion.

Key well results underscore the quality of our portfolio. In the Permian Basin, our core growth engine, standout performances came from our Delaware Wolfcamp pads in Lea and Eddy Counties, New Mexico. The Lightning Bolt 12H-15H four-well pad achieved average 30-day initial production rates of 1,450 boe per day, with a 68% oil cut and EURs north of 1.2 million boe per well based on our Type Curve 3.0 analogs. These wells featured 3.2-mile laterals, 50-stage completions with 3,500 pounds of proppant per foot, and our proprietary cluster-tight design, which reduced uneven frac propagation by 25% per our microseismic data. Drilling costs averaged $6.8 million per well, a 12% reduction year-over-year, thanks to our pad drilling efficiencies and the rollout of our automated managed pressure drilling systems from NOV's Varco rigs.

In the Midland Basin, our Sunset Ridge 101H well in Upton County posted an IP30 of 1,120 boe per day at 72% oil, outperforming our Type Curve 2.5 by 15%. This reflects the stacked-pay potential in our 35,000-acre position, where we're delineating third-bench Wolfcamp and Spraberry intervals. Overall, Permian success rates held at 98% this quarter, with cycle times down to 65 days from spud to first sales—among the best in the peer set.

In Eagle Ford, South Texas operations delivered from the Karnes Pride 7H well in Karnes County, with an IP30 of 950 boe per day, 55% condensate cut, and an EUR of 850,000 boe. We're leveraging hybrid slickwater-linear gel completions to boost propped fracture lengths by 20%, and we've reduced water cuts to under 40% through better diverter tech from Liberty Oilfield Services. This basin generates high-margin barrels, with breakevens around $45 WTI.

Offshore, Gulf of Mexico gained momentum. The Albatross #3 appraisal well in Green Canyon confirmed a 150-foot oil column in Miocene sands, with flow rates exceeding 5,000 bbl per day of 38-degree API crude during drill-stem testing. This de-risks a 100-million-barrel resource, advancing subsea tie-backs to our Neptune infrastructure, partnering with Shell. Deepwater capex here is modest at $150 million for the year, positioning for 20%+ IRRs at current Brent.

Internationally, our 15% carried interest in Namibia's Orange Basin Venus complex with TotalEnergies and QatarEnergy saw positives from Venus-2X, encountering 85 meters of high-quality reservoir with 25% porosity and oil shows. This aligns with super-giant potential akin to Guyana's Liza.

Technically, we've deployed AI-driven sweet spotting via TGS and Schlumberger's Petrel, increasing success rates with 10% higher EUR locations in Permian. Cube development pilots slash interference by 30%, boosting economics. All-electric frack fleets from ProFrac cut Scope 1 emissions by 40%, below 0.2 methane intensity.

For future plans, Q4 spuds 30 wells, full-year 115 skewed 70% Permian D&C. D&C inventory at 1,800 locations, 60% Tier 1, half-life to 15 years via lease swaps and bolt-ons like $200 million Northern Delaware adding 120 locations at $15,000 per acre. Capex flexible; at $75 WTI, $1.2 billion FCF funds program, returning 50% via buybacks and dividend. Hedged 60% 2025 oil at $72. Risks like frac sand up 8% mitigated by contracts with Halliburton and Patterson-UTI. Advancing carbon capture with Occidental's STRATOS.

These results validate high-grading: better rocks, tech, costs, returns.

Now I will turn it over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for an update on our exploration activities.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Maria. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 30 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Tom Reilly to discuss our marketing strategy.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for renewable diesel blends in the Gulf Coast market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of these low-carbon products is significant, commanding premiums and supporting our sustainability goals.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on exploration and drilling activity updates?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, John. Happy to elaborate. As Maria outlined, our Q3 drilling executed with discipline across high-return assets, spudding 28 and online 32 wells. Permian highlights like Lightning Bolt pads with 1,450 boe/d IP30 and Midland's Sunset Ridge outperforming type curves show portfolio strength. Eagle Ford and Gulf of Mexico Albatross appraisal de-risk major resources, while Namibia Venus updates build excitement. Future plans prioritize 115 annual wells, extending inventory to 15 years. All supported by tech like AI sweet spotting and electric fleets cutting emissions.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for ESG initiatives progress on emissions reduction targets?

Steve Harlan: Good morning, Lisa. ESG is core to our license to operate and value creation. Year-to-date through Q3, we've achieved a 28% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions intensity to 18.2 tCO2e per boe from 25.4 in 2019 baseline—tracking toward 45-50% absolute cut by 2030 and net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2050. Absolute Scope 1&2 down 12% YoY to 32.4 million tCO2e despite 5% production growth. Methane intensity slashed 55% to 0.18% of gas, 65% absolute drop via 15,000 continuous monitors, FLIR, GHGSat—plugged 240 emitters in Permian. Flaring down 42% to 4.2 Bcf/d globally, Permian 68% via 12 recovery units generating $45 million revenue. Permian electrification on 65% fracs cuts N2O/CO2 18%, NextEra solar offsets 150,000 tCO2e. North Sea 95% electrified at 5.1 tCO2e/boe; Guyana subsea all-electric <10 kg/boe; ADNOC CCUS injecting 1.2 MtCO2/year. Digital twins, airborne surveys, blue hydrogen add tech edge. Saved $220 million, unlocked $3.2 billion ESG financing. 2024 targets 30% intensity cut with $500 million capex.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: Could you please provide more color on capital expenditure breakdown?

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks, Mike. As Steve detailed, Q3 capex $620 million under $650 million budget. Drilling $355M vs $380M, Permian efficiencies with Schlumberger tech; completions $185M vs $200M, proppant savings and zipper fracs; facilities $80M over $70M on gathering and water but offset by deferrals. YTD underspend funds M&A, Q4 $580-620M.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Sarah. Exploration results like Albatross confirming 100 MMbbl and Namibia Venus de-risking billions directly shape strategy by extending inventory, lowering breakevens, and prioritizing Tier 1. Integrates with 2024 capex for 30 wells, blending high-probability with upside wildcats for organic growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Wong: What is the outlook for future development plans and resource potential?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, David. Our resource base is strong: PDP reserves 1.2 BBOE up 18%, total proved 2.8 BBOE (65% oil), 2P 5.1 BBOE, 3P 7.9 BBOE. Contingent 3.2 BBOE, 15+ years inventory at 450,000 boe/d. Permian 70% 2P, 3,200 locations EUR 1.4 MMboe, $40 breakeven, ramping to 320,000 boe/d. Eagle Ford 850 locations 900 MMboe EUR. Gulf Winterfell online Q4 2024 adds 25,000 boe/d, Blacktip wildcat 400 MMboe. Suriname 500 MMboe contingent. 2024 capex $2.8B funds 550 Permian wells, growth to 520,000 boe/d. AI sims, EOR pilots, electrification enhance. Hedged FCF $1.4B annual, ROCE 20%.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2023. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
